entries.clue: Sacked Eurosceptic, that is to say, revolutionary (9)

blocks.note: Sir Bill Cash, veteran Tory Eurosceptic MP

annotation.surface: A Eurosceptic politician has been fired, and the clue spells out that he was a revolutionary.
annotation.walkthrough: Bill Cash was a long-serving Conservative MP famous for opposing the EU, so the surface's sacked Eurosceptic is a real type of Westminster figure.
annotation.definitionFit: A military word: an officer dismissed from the service in disgrace is cashiered, which extends to anyone sacked.

entries.clue: Weeks spent on Democrat's debut – biased? (6)

indicatorNotes.spent: spent weeks are used up and broken apart, so the letters are rearranged
indicatorNotes.debut: a debut is a first appearance, so take the first letter

annotation.surface: Someone asks whether weeks of coverage lavished on a Democrat's first outing amount to bias.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Spent' reads as time passed in the surface but tells you to rearrange WEEKS with the D.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: something set at a slant rather than straight, figuratively a report leaning one way.

entries.clue: Tender arse enclosed in raunchy fringes (8)

indicatorNotes.in: ENC goes in, between the fringe letters
indicatorNotes.fringes: the fringes of a word are its outside letters, like the fringe on a rug

blocks.note: an arse, as an insult, is a contemptible person: a cur
enc. is the abbreviation for enclosed, as at the foot of a letter

annotation.surface: A cheeky picture of a sore backside tucked inside racy frilly underwear.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Tender' wants to mean sore, next to 'arse'; it is money, as in legal tender. Arse as an insult for a person is British slang.
annotation.definitionFit: Legal tender is the money a creditor must accept, so tender on its own stands for money in circulation.

entries.clue: A bloody alternative route! (6)

annotation.definitionNote: 'A bloody' stands for a bloody operation, a heart bypass

blocks.note: a bloody one, that is, heart surgery that reroutes the blood
a road built to carry traffic around a town

annotation.surface: An exasperated driver curses a detour.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Bloody' looks like a driver's swear word; it is really the surgical sense, a heart operation being a bloody business.
annotation.definitionFit: The word names both a ring road around a town and the surgery that sends blood round a blocked artery.

entries.clue: Modern art? Remove! (8)

annotation.definitionNote: 'Modern art' stands for a kind of modern art, the non-representational kind

blocks.note: twentieth-century painting of shapes and colours rather than recognisable things
a formal verb for taking something out

annotation.surface: A gallery-goer faced with modern art demands it be taken away.
annotation.walkthrough: The verb, stressed on its second syllable, means to take out or extract, as in abstracting a summary from a paper.
annotation.definitionFit: Two senses: non-representational art, and a formal verb for extracting or taking away.

entries.clue: Conservatives just started to get in correct order? (5)

indicatorNotes.just started: only the start of Conservatives is used, its first letter
indicatorNotes.to get in: C gets in, goes inside, EDIT

annotation.surface: The Conservatives, barely begun, are trying to get into proper order.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Correct order' reads as one phrase but splits: correct is EDIT, order is the definition.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: a decree issued by an authority is an order in the commanding sense, not the tidy one.

entries.clue: What some UK cities face, as reckless extreme wings of party turn back (10)

indicatorNotes.reckless: reckless letters behave wildly, so rearrange them
indicatorNotes.extreme wings: the extreme wings of a word are its first and last letters

blocks.note: first and last letters of PartY

annotation.surface: Cities face a crisis while a party's wings recklessly retreat.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Turn back' looks like a reversal instruction, but it is simply letters to be mixed. Several UK councils, including Birmingham, have declared themselves effectively bust.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by example: several British city councils have issued notices admitting they cannot pay their way.

entries.clue: European leader replaced with time (depression) (6)

indicatorNotes.leader replaced with: the leader of a word is its first letter, and it is swapped out for another

blocks.note: FRENCH with its leader F taken out

annotation.surface: A European leader's replacement brings time for depression.
annotation.walkthrough: 'European leader' is not a head of state: it is the first letter of a word for European.
annotation.definitionFit: A depression in the physical sense: a long narrow hollow dug or worn into the ground.

entries.clue: Wait – presidential candidate name to be taken off! (4)

indicatorNotes.to be taken off: a name taken off a list or ballot is removed, so the letter for name goes

blocks.note: the Democrat who stood aside as candidate in 2024
N = name; this letter is removed

annotation.surface: A plea to pause while a presidential candidate's name is struck off the ballot.
annotation.walkthrough: The surface recalls Joe Biden standing down in 2024, which is exactly what the wordplay does to his name: BIDEN loses N.
annotation.definitionFit: An old-fashioned verb for staying or waiting, surviving mostly in the idiom about biding one's time.

entries.clue: One who reveals broadcaster takes heroin (6)

blocks.note: a sower broadcasts seed, scattering it by hand

annotation.surface: A whistleblower exposes a broadcaster's heroin use.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Broadcaster' suggests the BBC; its older sense is scattering seed, so a broadcaster is a sower. Read the answer as show-er, not the rain.
annotation.definitionFit: A crossword-only sense: the verb show plus -er, one who shows, rather than the rain or the wash.

entries.clue: Nigel (as Tice?) able to endure a stretch inside (7)

indicatorNotes.inside: the answer lies inside the run of letters

annotation.surface: Nigel Farage, standing in for Richard Tice, could survive a spell in prison.
annotation.walkthrough: Richard Tice is Farage's Reform UK deputy. 'A stretch' sounds like jail time, but here it is literal.
annotation.definitionFit: A descriptive definition: material that can be pulled out and spring back without breaking.

entries.clue: (& 22ac.) Useless wanker is late meeting court date (4)

annotation.surface: A useless tosser turns up late for his day in court.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Court' and 'date' look like a legal appointment, but court is the romantic verb and date is only its abbreviation. The answer runs on into 22 across.
annotation.definitionFit: An idiom from forestry: branches that bear nothing, applied to staff who contribute nothing to an organisation.

entries.clue: Capital is in a mess: company needs to be incorporated (7)

indicatorNotes.in a mess: letters in a mess are jumbled
indicatorNotes.needs to be incorporated: CO must be taken into the body of the jumble

annotation.surface: A capital's finances are in disarray and a company must be formed.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Capital' tempts as money in this business surface; it is a capital city. The 'in a' that looks like part of 'is in a mess' is itself fodder.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by example: the seat of government of Cyprus, divided between the Greek and Turkish sides.

entries.clue: "Grass currently playing well," TV presenter (9)

blocks.note: in form = playing well at the moment
Ant McPartlin, of the TV duo Ant and Dec

annotation.surface: A TV presenter praises someone called Grass for a good run of form.
annotation.walkthrough: Ant and Dec are Britain's best-known TV presenting duo.
annotation.definitionFit: British slang: a grass is someone who tells the police about criminals, from rhyming slang grasshopper for copper.

entries.clue: Gives away drawers after live introduction (7)

indicatorNotes.after: after means following in sequence, so the drawers follow the word for live
indicatorNotes.introduction: an introduction is what comes first, so the word for live opens the answer

blocks.note: sliding drawers in a cabinet are trays

annotation.surface: Someone hands over a chest of drawers after a live launch event.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Drawers' suggests furniture or knickers; the trays inside a cabinet are the letters needed.
annotation.definitionFit: Giving away a secret or a friend is the treacherous sense; it can also mean simply revealing, as a blush does.

entries.clue: "English taken in by Archer's falsification" : investigate (8)

indicatorNotes.taken in by: E is taken inside the other letters
indicatorNotes.falsification: falsifying the letters of ARCHERS rearranges them

annotation.surface: A call to investigate English deceived by Jeffrey Archer's lies.
annotation.walkthrough: Jeffrey Archer, novelist and Tory peer, was jailed for perjury, so 'falsification' fits his name.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym, as a verb: to study a subject closely to establish facts.

entries.clue: Distant object, not hard, acting as a windbreaker (7)

indicatorNotes.not: H is not wanted, so it is dropped from THING

annotation.surface: A remote, soft object is being used as a screen against the wind.
annotation.walkthrough: A windbreaker sounds like a screen on the beach; here it is someone breaking wind.
annotation.definitionFit: A cryptic twist on the idiom break wind: a windbreaker is taken literally as one who breaks wind.

entries.clue: Everything associated with Rees-Mogg's position in the party is OK? (3,5)

blocks.note: Jacob Rees-Mogg sits on the right of the Conservative Party

annotation.surface: A sardonic question whether everything to do with Rees-Mogg's place in the party is fine.
annotation.walkthrough: Jacob Rees-Mogg, the Conservative MP and minister, is a figurehead of the party's right wing.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: both are everyday words for satisfactory or acceptable, and the question mark fits the enquiring sense.

entries.clue: Draw produces Sunak supporter, say, harbouring glimmer (of hope?) (6)

indicatorNotes.harbouring: CON harbours, holds inside it, RAY

blocks.note: a ray of hope is a glimmer

annotation.surface: A contest ends in a draw, leaving a Sunak supporter clinging to a glimmer of hope.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Draw' looks like a tied result or a noun; it is the verb.
annotation.definitionFit: The stick of coloured wax doubles as a verb: to make a picture with one.

entries.clue: More than one cut by the state (7)

annotation.surface: More than one thing has been cut by the government.
annotation.walkthrough: 'The state' reads as government cuts; it is a US state abbreviation.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: a determiner for a number above one but not many.

entries.clue: Naive move to acquire new capital (6)

indicatorNotes.move: the letters of NAIVE move about

annotation.surface: A naive plan to buy new capital, as in funds.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Capital' again suggests money; it is a capital city.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by example: Austria's seat of government on the Danube.

entries.clue: see 12ac. (4)
Evasive politician's words he might have to eat? (6)

annotation.definitionNote: 'he might have to eat' stands for something one eats, a noun

blocks.note: long-winded talk that avoids saying anything definite

annotation.surface: A politician who dodged questions may end up eating his words.
annotation.walkthrough: The surface plays on eating one's words: the politician's evasive talk can also be a breakfast item.
annotation.definitionFit: Two senses: wordy talk with no substance, and the batter cake cooked in a gridded iron.

entries.clue: Technique offering an opportunity to get your leg over, it's said (5)

indicatorNotes.it's said: what is said is heard rather than read, so the word only has to sound right

blocks.clueFragment: offering an opportunity to get your leg over
blocks.note: a stile is a step for climbing over a fence

annotation.surface: A technique for getting lucky in bed.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Get your leg over' is British slang for having sex; here it means swinging a leg over the steps set into a field fence.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: a characteristic manner of doing something, as in a swimmer's stroke or a writer's voice.

entries.clue: Get Yard organised? Disaster! (7)

indicatorNotes.organised: the letters are organised into a new order

annotation.surface: A cry to sort out Scotland Yard, which is a disaster.
annotation.walkthrough: The Yard is Scotland Yard, London's Metropolitan Police headquarters.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: a calamitous event, borrowing the name of the drama that ends in catastrophe.

entries.clue: Intelligence reduced May's dubious shame (6)

indicatorNotes.reduced: INFO is cut short, losing its last letter
indicatorNotes.dubious: MAY's letters are dubious, so rearrange them

blocks.note: INFO, information, without its last letter

annotation.surface: Reports about Theresa May's questionable disgrace.
annotation.walkthrough: 'May' looks like Theresa May, the former Prime Minister; she is only three letters to mix.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: notoriety for something bad, the public disgrace of a bad reputation.

entries.clue: Political alliance head: "Keir's first to go!" (4)

indicatorNotes.first: only Keir's first letter, K, is meant
indicatorNotes.to go: to go means to leave, so that letter leaves the word for head

blocks.note: block is slang for head, as in knock your block off

annotation.surface: An alliance leader demands that Keir Starmer be first out.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Head' looks like the leader of the alliance; it is the slang for the skull.
annotation.definitionFit: Borrowed from French: a group of parties or nations voting or acting together, as in the Eastern one.

entries.clue: Offhand Macron's negative election loser breaks into song (10)

indicatorNotes.breaks into: AL breaks into CHANT, landing inside it

blocks.note: Al Gore, who lost the 2000 US presidential election

annotation.surface: Macron's casual 'non' as a defeated candidate bursts into song.
annotation.walkthrough: Macron is French, so his no is NON.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym from French: coolly unconcerned, casual in manner.
